title: Origin and classification of fractional dynamical topology in non-Hermitian quantum systems
authors: Zimiao Zhang, Li Chen, Weilun Jiang, Heng Shen
abstract: Dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPT) provide a fundamental framework for characterizing nonequilibrium critical phenomena, and have recently been extended to non-Hermitian systems. Half-integer jumps of the dynamical topological order parameter can arise in both Hermitian and non-Hermitian systems, yet their origin in non-Hermitian settings remains unclear. Here, we investigate DQPTs in a two-band non-Hermitian model and show that these fractional jumps originate from the discontinuity in the complex energy spectrum. We demonstrate that this behavior is intrinsically linked to the steady-state phase diagram of the quench Hamiltonian, and also classify the occurrence of DQPT. We further extend our analysis to the multiband Hamiltonian and the two-dimensional model, providing a unified understanding of fractional dynamical topological signatures.
summary: This paper characterizes dynamical quantum phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems by analyzing the Dynamical Topological Order Parameter (DTOP). It proves that the characteristic half-integer quantization of this parameter arises fundamentally from discontinuities in the complex energy spectrum. This provides a unified, topological understanding of non-equilibrium criticality applicable to various non-Hermitian models.
main_problem: The paper investigates the origin and classification of fractional dynamical topology in non-Hermitian quantum systems, specifically focusing on half-integer jumps of the dynamical topological order parameter (DTOP).
main_result: The half-integer DTOP jumps in non-Hermitian systems originate from the discontinuity in the complex energy spectrum, distinguishing them fundamentally from the integer jumps seen in Hermitian systems.
method: The analysis uses the Loschmidt echo and defines the DTOP based on the phase winding of the system's evolution operator across critical momenta.
model_or_system: The study employs a two-band non-Hermitian model, exemplified by the non-Hermitian Su–Schrieffer–Heeger (SSH) model, and extends to multiband and two-dimensional Haldane models.
key_observables: Dynamical Topological Order Parameter (DTOP), Loschmidt echo, complex energy spectrum, and phase winding ($\Delta\phi$).
important_parameters: Quench parameters ($\eta, \gamma, \delta$), critical momenta ($k_j$), and time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the biorthogonal framework and assumes the system undergoes a sudden quench from an initial to a final Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams, comparing integer jumps (Hermitian) with half-integer jumps (non-Hermitian) in the DTOP, and show the evolution of the DTOP in 2D systems via phase winding.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining DQPTs in non-Hermitian systems using a 1D model, establishing the link between half-integer jumps and spectral discontinuities, and finally generalizing the concept to 2D systems using phase winding integrals.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous, topological characterization of non-equilibrium critical phenomena in non-Hermitian settings, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
